answer_text:
Let

\[
f(X)=X^4+2X+1,\qquad d(X)=X^2-2X+2.
\]

Since \(a\) is a root of \(f\), two polynomials that are congruent modulo \(f(X)\) take the same value at \(a\). We want a polynomial \(p(X)\in\mathbb{Q}[X]\) with \(\deg p<4\) such that

\[
d(X)p(X)\equiv X+1 \pmod{f(X)}.
\]

Write

\[
p(X)=c_3X^3+c_2X^2+c_1X+c_0.
\]

Then

\[
\begin{aligned}
d(X)p(X)
&=(X^2-2X+2)(c_3X^3+c_2X^2+c_1X+c_0)\\
&=c_3X^5+(c_2-2c_3)X^4+(c_1-2c_2+2c_3)X^3\\
&\qquad +(c_0-2c_1+2c_2)X^2+(-2c_0+2c_1)X+2c_0.
\end{aligned}
\]

Using \(X^4\equiv -2X-1\) and \(X^5\equiv -2X^2-X\) modulo \(f(X)\), this becomes

\[
\begin{aligned}
d(X)p(X)\equiv &(c_1-2c_2+2c_3)X^3 \\
&+(c_0-2c_1+2c_2-2c_3)X^2 \\
&+(-2c_0+2c_1-2c_2+3c_3)X \\
&+(2c_0-c_2+2c_3)
\end{aligned}
\pmod{f(X)}.
\]

We need this to equal \(X+1\). Thus

\[
\begin{cases}
c_1-2c_2+2c_3=0,\\
c_0-2c_1+2c_2-2c_3=0,\\
-2c_0+2c_1-2c_2+3c_3=1,\\
2c_0-c_2+2c_3=1.
\end{cases}
\]

From the first two equations,

\[
c_1=2c_2-2c_3,\qquad c_0=2c_2-2c_3,
\]

so \(c_0=c_1\). The last two equations become

\[
\begin{cases}
-2c_2+3c_3=1,\\
3c_2-2c_3=1.
\end{cases}
\]

Solving gives \(c_2=1\) and \(c_3=1\). Hence

\[
c_0=c_1=0.
\]

Therefore

\[
p(X)=X^3+X^2.
\]

Indeed,

\[
(X^2-2X+2)(X^3+X^2)-(X+1)=(X-1)(X^4+2X+1).
\]

Since \(f(a)=0\),

\[
(a^2-2a+2)(a^3+a^2)=a+1.
\]

The denominator is nonzero for a root \(a\), so

\[
\frac{a+1}{a^2-2a+2}=a^3+a^2.
\]

\[
\boxed{a^3+a^2}
\]
